evidence: DEFINING BEHAVIOUR IS GRADED: the brief's core is a shared pipeline board with one-stage moves, interview places, stale-move refusal naming who, all-or-none bulk moves with undo, live updates, and per-application conversations with unread/seen/drafts and candidate privacy (instruction.md:3-9). Functional judge.toml grades every one of these as separate binary rows: hro_move_one_stage (w1.5), hro_reorder (1.5), hro_interview_full (1.5), hro_stale_refused (2.5), hro_bulk_move (1.5), hro_bulk_all_or_none (2), hro_undo_restores (2), hro_undo_conflict (2), hro_live_board (2.5), hro_msg_exchange (1.5), hro_unread_counts (2), hro_seen (1.5), hro_drafts (2), hro_candidate_private (2.5); polish adds hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread (w3 each). SERVER-BACKED (not merely same-origin): constraints gate hro_gate_shared requires a job + candidate created through the UI and then found by the Observer 'in a new independent empty browser context', and explicitly says 'A static seed response, a no-op success message, a browser-only save or a job-only app does not satisfy the gate' (gates/constraints/judge.toml criterion description); the functional and polish prompts repeat this as a global browser gate that zeroes every binary row on failure, and define independence as browser.newContext() ('A reload or a second tab of the same context is not independent'). Further cross-context server readbacks: hro_reorder ('the new order is what an independent context of another recruiter sees'), hro_add_candidate, hro_job_open, C protocol (Mei Lin in independent context), hro_msg_exchange (Tomas's independent context), hro_notes (Aud in independent context reads notes), hro_activity (Observer reads same lines). A localStorage-only or in-tab app fails the gate. RELOAD / RE-AUTH: hro_drafts covers reload; polish hro_pol_session_resume (w2.5) covers the brief's 'get signed out; when I sign back in it is still there, and nobody else who signs in on that browser sees it' (instruction.md:7; hireops_rules.md:168-175) including Mei seeing empty boxes and Rafael's drafts surviving her visit; drafts' storage location is left to the builder ('Where drafts are kept is yours'), so not requiring server-side drafts is correct and not a hidden requirement. Fresh sign-in readbacks in independent contexts cover hireops_rules.md:59 'Order survives a reload, a fresh sign-in and a restart'. RESTART: hro_restart (w1.5) with protocol D: record jobs, card order per stage, notes, last messages, activity lines and seeded Platform Engineer order/note from Z, call restart_app once, sign in again and compare; fails if anything lost/reordered/duplicated or 'the starting data is not loaded again' is violated; 'A reload is not a restart; if restart_app reports an error or cannot be called, hro_restart is 0'. The restart tool is wired in functional/judge.toml ([[judge.mcp_servers]] verifier -> /tests/tools/restart_mcp.py $APP_RESTART_HELPER); test.sh:127-193 (template-identical) kills the process group and relaunches node over the same DB_PATH as uid 65534, single-use marker cleared at :192; suites run sequentially (run_suite with --max-concurrent-agent 1), so the restart cannot race another dimension. Golden is genuinely durable: db.js:7-20 uses better-sqlite3 at process.env.DB_PATH and documents 'a database that already holds users is never reseeded'. Scripted golden evidence (hash-verified, explicitly not a judge run): workspace.json groups 23 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages and activity without reseeding; live updates resume' passed, 21 'session ended mid-draft ... same person resumes and sends; another person sees no draft' passed, 19 drafts across switch and reload passed, 17 live board passed. BROKEN-APP PROBES: (a) localStorage/in-memory-per-tab app -> fails shared gate, all binaries 0; (b) server keeps state in RAM only -> passes gate and cross-context rows but hro_restart = 0 (correct, bounded by weight); (c) app that reseeds on every boot -> passes cross-context rows but hro_restart fails on duplicated/reset seed and lost work; (d) app that hides drafts in a shared, unkeyed localStorage -> hro_pol_session_resume fails because Mei sees Rafael's draft. CONFORMING ALTERNATIVES: server-side drafts, SSE vs polling vs websocket, different routes - all accepted (rules let draft storage and transport be the builder's choice; prompts forbid assuming routes). No conforming design found that this row's criteria would fail for durability reasons. Minor NOTE (not a defect for this row): read markers/unread counts are not re-read after restart in hro_restart (it lists jobs, order, notes, messages, activity); the brief's 'keep new work across restarts' durability is still proven by several state classes, so the 'at least one criterion' bar is met. RISK FLAG REASON: no full configured judge run, Oracle grade or hosted QC exists for these exact bytes (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'); whether the configured claude-code judge actually invokes restart_app and the newContext() independent-context probe within budget is unmeasured, so the design-level Pass is not runtime-confirmed.
